verdict.rationale: Channel3 is an API-first product. It documents a /v1 public API with per-endpoint reference pages and a live 'Try it' runner, and publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec (48 paths plus webhooks). It also offers free API keys with no OAuth flow, plus an SDK and a CLI that wrap the API, and a semver changelog with migration notes. The probe 404s were at different docs.trychannel3.com paths, so they do not contradict the published spec. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of the API docs' completeness, and a formal versioning/deprecation-notice policy (the OpenAPI info block also still carries framework-default metadata).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: Access 100 million+ products from 25,000+ brands through one API.
Channel3 publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 document (48 paths plus 5 webhooks, production server https://api.trychannel3.com)
The Mintlify-hosted API reference runs the "Try it" playground per endpoint
No OAuth flow is required for the public product data API. API keys are free to create.
The Channel3 CLI calls the Channel3 API from a terminal or script.
